2.translation: ## What do you want to plot? ⟦shared:0⟧

3.translation: | I want to… | Read the guide | Try a plot |

5.translation: | Compare sequence order, annotations and interval links | [Multi-sequence relationships](⟦shared:0⟧) | [Start with sequence backbones](⟦shared:1⟧) |

6.translation: | Show features and tracks along one circular sequence | [Single-sequence circular maps](⟦shared:0⟧) | [Start with lengths and known annotations](⟦shared:1⟧) |

7.translation: | Inspect local alignments on two axes | [Alignment dot plots](⟦shared:0⟧) | [Draw HSP endpoints and directions](⟦shared:1⟧) |

8.translation: | Combine an overview, a magnified region or different views | [Multi-view composition](⟦shared:0⟧) | [Combine and connect two plots](⟦shared:1⟧) |

9.translation: Browse the [example gallery](⟦shared:0⟧) by plot type or task for reproducible examples.

11.translation: ## Which layout should I use to compare sequences? ⟦shared:0⟧

14.translation: Show sequences and their links along curved backbones. See [backbone shape, curvature and radius](⟦shared:0⟧).

17.translation: Arrange sequences in rows or columns to compare gene order, anchors and local regions. See [alignment and arrangement](⟦shared:0⟧).

20.translation: Arrange sequences as spokes, keeping their own coordinates and showing syntenic relationships in the center. See [radial layout](⟦shared:0⟧).

23.translation: Place sequences in query and subject columns and show observed interval relationships with ribbons. See [two-column layout](⟦shared:0⟧).

26.translation: Arrange features, primers, restriction sites or quantitative tracks along a single circular sequence. See [single-sequence circular maps](⟦shared:0⟧).

29.translation: [Dotplot](⟦shared:0⟧) shows paired HSP endpoints on two sequence axes. [Fusion](⟦shared:1⟧) arranges independent plots and can connect them through the source intervals they display.

31.translation: ## What do you want to adjust? ⟦shared:0⟧

34.translation: | Adjust arrow shapes and placement | [Feature shapes](⟦shared:0⟧) and [overlapping annotations](⟦shared:1⟧) |

35.translation: | Handle crowded labels | [Text fitting and repulsion](⟦shared:0⟧) |

36.translation: | Add signals, coverage or other quantitative tracks | [Tracks](⟦shared:0⟧) and [track statistics](⟦shared:1⟧) |

37.translation: | Set colors, legends or themes | [Layer styling](⟦shared:0⟧) and [scales](⟦shared:1⟧) |

38.translation: | Set geometry separately by sequence or strand | [Argument formats](⟦shared:0⟧) |

39.translation: | Save at a target size or troubleshoot the layout | [Output](⟦shared:0⟧) and [diagnostics](⟦shared:1⟧) |

44.translation: | Reference data | Supplies sequence IDs, lengths and units | ⟦shared:0⟧ |

45.translation: | Geometric layers | Draw backbones, links, features, tracks and text | ⟦shared:0⟧ |

46.translation: | Mapping | Connects fields to visual aesthetics | ⟦shared:0⟧ |

47.translation: | Scales | Set how values and legends appear | ⟦shared:0⟧ |

48.translation: | Local positions | Arrange features, labels and tracks | ⟦shared:0⟧ |

49.translation: | Coordinates | Set the overall layout of a plot | ⟦shared:0⟧ |

50.translation: | Theme | Sets fonts, spacing and other non-data appearance | ⟦shared:0⟧ |

53.translation: Source IDs, coordinate units and full sequence lengths come from the input. A source can have multiple display instances, and display orientation can be set independently. DNA uses bp and proteins use aa. To move between them, use an [explicit coordinate projection](⟦shared:0⟧).

58.translation: [Install ggchord and draw a first plot](⟦shared:0⟧). To use your own tables, see the [essential fields and coordinate conventions](⟦shared:1⟧).
